title: Path Existence Queries in a Graph II
summary: Given an integer n representing the number of nodes in a graph, labeled from 0 to n - 1, along with an integer array nums of length n and an integer maxDiff, an undirected edge exists between nodes i and j if the absolute difference between nums[i] and nums[j] is at most maxDiff (i.e., |nums[i] - nums[j]| <= maxDiff).
statement: Given an integer n representing the number of nodes in a graph, labeled from 0 to n - 1, along with an integer array nums of length n and an integer maxDiff, an undirected edge exists between nodes i and j if the absolute difference between nums[i] and nums[j] is at most maxDiff (i.e., |nums[i] - nums[j]| <= maxDiff). For each query [ui, vi], determine the minimum distance between nodes ui and vi. If no path exists between the two nodes, return -1 for that query. Return an array of results corresponding to each query.
constraints: nums has n values with n up to 100,000; nodes are joined when their value difference is at most max_diff.
Edges are unweighted and queries ask shortest path length, with zero for the same node and -1 if disconnected.
reference_solution:
def minimum_threshold_graph_distances(n,nums,max_diff,queries):
    ordered=sorted((value,index) for index,value in enumerate(nums));rank=[0]*n
    for position,(_,index) in enumerate(ordered):rank[index]=position
    next_position=[0]*n;right=0
    for left in range(n):
        right=max(right,left)
        while right+1<n and ordered[right+1][0]-ordered[left][0]<=max_diff:right+=1
        next_position[left]=right
    levels=max(1,n.bit_length());jump=[next_position]
    for _ in range(1,levels):jump.append([jump[-1][jump[-1][i]] for i in range(n)])
    answer=[]
    for source,target in queries:
        if source==target:answer.append(0);continue
        left,right=sorted((rank[source],rank[target]));steps=0;current=left
        for level in range(levels-1,-1,-1):
            nxt=jump[level][current]
            if nxt<right and nxt>current:current=nxt;steps+=1<<level
        answer.append(steps+1 if next_position[current]>=right else -1)
    return answer

tests.explanation: Each queried pair differs by at most three, so both shortest paths use one edge.
The answers include a direct edge, a two-hop chain, a disconnected pair, and another direct edge.
